name: world-openfoodfacts
description: Open Food Facts (world.openfoodfacts.org) is an open, crowd-sourced food products database. This CLI reads product detail pages and their related data (Robotoff questions, folksonomy tags), the reference lists (countries, food-preference attribute groups, preference levels, external knowledge sources) and the bulk data-dump links.

commands.name: get-product
commands.summary: Get a food product's name, common name and Nutri-Score breakdown by barcode (EAN/UPC), parsed from its product page

commands.name: get-product-questions
commands.summary: List the Robotoff machine-generated questions (for example a suggested category or label to confirm) that are pending for a product barcode

params.name: lang
params.description: Language code for the question text, e.g. en, fr

commands.name: list-countries
commands.summary: List the countries Open Food Facts supports, as a map from country code (e.g. us, fr) to English country name

commands.name: list-attribute-groups
commands.summary: List the product attribute groups used for personalized ranking (nutritional quality, processing, allergens, environment, …) with their attributes and allowed values

commands.name: list-preference-levels
commands.summary: List the importance levels a user can assign to a product attribute (not important, important, very important, mandatory) with their scoring factors

commands.name: list-external-sources
commands.summary: List the external knowledge-panel providers (for example the animal-welfare Suffering Footprint) and the product filters each one applies to

params.name: lc
params.description: Language code for names and descriptions, e.g. en, fr

commands.name: list-data-exports
commands.summary: List the nightly database dump and export downloads (MongoDB dump, CSV, JSONL, …) with their download and checksum links

notes: No anonymous search or listing is available. robots.txt blocks keyword search (/cgi/search.pl) and the /api/v2/product JSON API. Category, brand and facet listings (/facets/..., /category/...) redirect or return 503 'not available to anonymous users'. To find a product you need its barcode.
get-product requests /product/{barcode}, and the site redirects that to the canonical /product/{barcode}/{slug} page. Fields are scraped from the server-rendered HTML.
Within a get-product result, the first panel title is the overall Nutri-Score grade and the matching span is its summary.

get-product-questions and get-product-folksonomy often return empty results: questions:[] with status 'no_questions', or []. Both recorded barcodes returned empty, so an empty response is normal rather than an error.
Prefer the bulk dumps from list-data-exports for large-scale data. The data is licensed under ODbL and needs attribution.
